impact_scope.description: A new public C API constructs a PLIST_DATE from a caller-supplied int64_t UNIX timestamp.

evidence: S0 has no matching declaration for plist_new_unix_date; the selected declaration context explicitly reports no match.
Because this exact public entry point did not exist in S0, it had no S0 harness-exposure obligation.
S1 declares and implements plist_new_unix_date(int64_t sec).
H0 only invokes plist_from_bin, plist_from_json, plist_from_openstep, and plist_from_xml, followed by plist_free; it never calls plist_new_unix_date or supplies its int64_t timestamp argument.

new_harness_obligation.description: H0 must add a direct call to plist_new_unix_date and construct an int64_t UNIX timestamp from fuzz-controlled input to expose this new public API.
evidence: The new API requires a caller-supplied int64_t sec value.
None of the existing harness entry points supplies that value or invokes this constructor.

reason: The anchored unit is the newly introduced public plist_new_unix_date entry point. Its same-scope gap is false in S0 because the declaration is absent and true in S1 because unchanged H0 does not call it. This creates a concrete new harness call and input-construction obligation, so the delta is NEW and maintenance is needed.
